newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Airlines firmer after cash news.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Airlines firmer after cash news.

text.p: Shares of Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) opened firmer on Monday after it announced a 3.27 billion ringgit fund-raising exercise over the weekend.
After around an hour of trading, the stock was up 25 cents to 6.65 ringgit.
"The market had expected a big fund-raising exercise at some time. Now it is out of the way," said Amerjit Chinna, an analyst at brokers BZW.
"It lifts a cloud of uncertainty. Sentiment has improved slightly and the company is now aware of some of the problems it faces," he said.
MAS on Sunday announced it would raise 3.271 billion ringgit through a one-for-one bonus issue, a one-for-one rights issue and a 1.5 billion ringgit bond issue.
MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli said the exercise was to help finance its aircraft acquisitions and investment in new facilities at the new Kuala LUmpur International Airport
The airline will receive its first Boeing 777-200 aircraft in April and at least three other aircraft this year.
"I think it's within our expectations, we expected them to do capital raising anyway," said a research manager at a foreign broking house in Kuala Lumpur. "The funds are cheap."
"But overall I don't see any good news because the earnings are diluted. But they have new funds, cheap funds," the research manager added.
